_about: NEX sentience-layer dependency DAG. Each node lists its prerequisites (edges pointing IN) and status. The build order is the topological sort of this graph. A node is 'buildable now' iff every prereq is 'built'. Run nex_next_dev.py to compute what's buildable / blocked / gap. This is the formal structure behind NEX_MIND_MAP_COMPLETE.md — the math the diagram visualizes.
_rule: buildable_now(node) := all(status[p] in ('built','live_unproven') for p in prereqs) and status[node]=='gap'. A live_unproven prereq is TREATED AS SATISFIED by the tool: dependents remain buildable and are tagged [LEANS ON UNPROVEN: ...] (nex_next_dev.py:79-81,102) — the tool FLAGS, it does not block. (Corrected 2026-10-11: the prior wording 'blocks ADVANCE until proven' described an intent the code never implemented; the project advanced to L4 over an unproven L3 deliberately — see L3_teeth_test note. To actually block, remove 'live_unproven' from _SATISFIED at nex_next_dev.py:29.)

L3_recursion.note: RECLASSIFIED built->live_unproven 2026-10-11 (the 'built' status overstated a test that could not separate hypothesis from null). COSMETIC — resolved pragmatically 2026-06-25. Teeth-test v2 gathered 258 real fire-samples: P(move|active)=0.333 vs P(move|absent)=0.337. Near-identical. Nudge fires only 1.2% of fires (raga rarely fixated after perseveration fix). Statistical resolution would take ~115 days. Honest verdict: prompt-hint nudge does not mechanically move attention. Recursion needs MECHANICAL teeth (retrieval weight shift on fixation) not a prompt hint. Proceeding to L4 — separate mechanism, does not depend on recursion working. Recursion mechanical fix is a parallel dev.

L3_teeth_test.note: RECLASSIFIED built->live_unproven 2026-10-11 (Beam, verified): this is the node that GATES L4_stakes (L4.prereqs=[L3_teeth_test]), and marking it 'built / Gate resolved' over a NULL overstated it. v2 built inline in generator.py (fire-event sampling, not timer), n=258 real samples, P(move|active)=0.333 vs P(move|absent)=0.337 — null at achievable sample (~115 days to resolve statistically). The test ran; the mechanism is unproven. L4 remains buildable but now correctly flags [LEANS ON UNPROVEN: L3_teeth_test].

L4_stakes.note: states the system cannot be neutral about — wired so deep they commandeer it. Mattering. The real frontier. CAVEAT 2026-10-11: L4 as built couples a bounded term to the readiness SCALAR, but readiness is saturated at fire time (96% of fires >=0.90; r80 §1c), so a <=0.20 term is decision-inert ~96% of the time — the volume-knob/prompt-hint analogue of the null L3 recursion. The scalar arm (r79 aversive / r80 reward) is NOT the live frontier; see L4_teeth.

L4_teeth.note: SELECTION-coupling frontier (added 2026-10-11, Beam Part 3; placement provisional). Where L4_stakes moves a readiness SCALAR (how OFTEN she fires — decision-inert, see L4_stakes caveat), L4_teeth shifts WHICH candidate leads WITHIN a fire: a retrieval-weight shift in global_workspace.arbitrate between candidate construction and max(), single-turn, no persistence. This is the mechanical-teeth lesson the L3 note already named ('needs MECHANICAL teeth not a prompt hint'). > L4 (moves selection, not a clamp-absorbed scalar); < L4b/L5 (no persistence, no felt claim). Falsifier: flag ON must change the LEADING candidate at matched cadence. Prereq L3_teeth_test = the teeth lineage; parallel to the L4_stakes scalar, not downstream of it. The persistent version is L4b_persistent_stake.
